images.title: A circle in 6 equal parts and one part folded in half
images.purpose: Show the circle in 6 equal parts, each a 1/6 turn, and one 1/6 part folded in half into two 1/12 parts, with how many 1/12 pieces cover 1/6, 2/6 and 3/6.
images.composition: A disc on the left with one 1/6 part split in two, and three short bars on the right showing the counts.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. DISC, centre (400, 410): a circle 500 px across with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (5 px) and a pale cream #FFF8E7 fill, cut by exactly 6 thin grey #6B7280 lines from the centre to the rim, one every 60 steps of the circle, so that there are exactly 6 equal parts; the first line goes to the right. The first part (just above the right-hand line) is filled amber #E69F00 and split in two equal halves by one dashed dark line from the centre to the rim, giving two small parts; each small part is labelled 1/12 (34 px, bold, dark) inside it. The other 5 parts are labelled 1/6 each (34 px, dark) near the rim. Starting point A is a teal #0072B2 dot 26 px across at the right end of the first line, with the letter A just outside. RIGHT SIDE, three rows, each a horizontal bar of identical small blocks, every block 60 px wide and 60 px high, amber #E69F00 with a thin dark outline and 6 px between blocks, starting at x 800: row 1 at y 250 has 2 blocks, row 2 at y 370 has 4 blocks, row 3 at y 490 has 6 blocks. Beside each row, to the right of its blocks, in dark bold sans-serif (40 px): 2 pieces of 1/12 make 1/6 after row 1 at x 960, 4 pieces of 1/12 make 2/6 after row 2 at x 1090, 6 pieces of 1/12 make 3/6 after row 3 at x 1220. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 6 equal parts in the circle
rows with a different number of blocks from 2, 4 and 6
images.takeaway: A 1/12 piece is half of a 1/6 piece, so 2, 4 and 6 pieces of 1/12 cover 1/6, 2/6 and 3/6.
images.description: A circle in 6 equal parts with the first part split into two 1/12 parts, and three rows of 1/12 blocks showing 2, 4 and 6 pieces.
images.context: Concept image for Measuring Turns in Sixths and Twelfths. It follows the idea of the circle folded in half and then into 3 equal parts, with one 1/6 part folded in half, in your maths book, and shows the concept's own count of 1/12 pieces.
images.teaching_notes: Count the 1/12 blocks in each row. The slip to watch is thinking 1/12 is bigger than 1/6 because 12 is bigger than 6.

image_decisions.why: The circle in 6 parts with one part halved and the rows of 1/12 blocks show why half of 1/6 is 1/12.
